key_insight: The paper shows that conventional FPV can decouple flamelet state from local strain, and proposes an $\varepsilon$-based coupling that ties the flamelet response more directly to the modeled turbulence field.
engineering_relevance: For reacting-flow CFD, the $\varepsilon$-$Z$ model offers a more physically consistent way to predict quenching, extinction, and product persistence in high-strain regions.
method: Ran 2D RANS simulations of a transonic accelerating reacting mixing layer.
Compared one-step chemistry, conventional FPV, and the proposed $\varepsilon$-$Z$ flamelet model.
Used $\varepsilon$ to infer flamelet strain rate $S^*$ and transported selected species explicitly.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparison against RANS-computed mean strain-rate fields, showing FPV preferentially samples near-equilibrium states in high-strain regions while the $\varepsilon$-$Z$ formulation better constrains flamelet state by local turbulence and flammability limits.
watch_item: The new coupling depends on modeled $\varepsilon$ and tabulated flamelet assumptions, so accuracy may be sensitive to turbulence-model fidelity and the reactant-availability scaling.
